solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Times keeping us hard at work

indicators.note: one piece keeping another holds it within itself

parts.note: 'by' expresses multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A newspaper keeps its staff toiling away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but stands for BY, as in multiplying; 'keeping' puts US inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone hard at work is occupied and fully engaged.

clue.text: Last resort to put up the money for station

parts.note: to back a venture is to fund it
a stop is a station on a rail or bus route

explanation.surface: Funding a railway station as a final option.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something kept in reserve as a final safeguard if all else fails.

clue.text: Small company with work that's exclusive

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A little firm producing something special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exclusive' is a noun here: a news story one paper has alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a news story published by one outlet ahead of rivals.

clue.text: Symbol kept shut up, left in the care of wizard

parts.note: pent, as in pent-up, means confined

indicators.note: being in someone's care means being held by them, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an ace or wizard is an expert

explanation.surface: A magic sign is locked away and entrusted to a sorcerer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' suggests magic, fitting the answer, but here it means an expert, ACE; 'in the care of' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a five-pointed star drawn in a circle, used as a magical emblem.

clue.text: Queen Richelieu has to make wealthy

indicators.note: the two names have the answer within them, spanning the word break

explanation.surface: A monarch needs the Cardinal Richelieu to make her rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make richer, give wealth or improve in value.

clue.text: Reference arranged at St Emilion

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reference set up at a famous Bordeaux wine town.
explanation.walkthrough: St Emilion is a wine town near Bordeaux.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a written statement vouching for someone's character, as for a job.

clue.text: Tear after mongrel that's in fashion

indicators.note: the tear is placed after the dog in the answer

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a rent is a tear or rip in cloth

explanation.surface: A rip appears after a stray dog runs past, now the latest look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' reads as weeping or racing but is a rip, RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: present-day and up to date, what is popular now.

clue.text: Still a number going topless

indicators.note: losing its top, the first letter of the number word is dropped

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A figure still going without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is the definition, used as in 'even better'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both intensify comparisons, as in 'still bigger' or 'even bigger'.

clue.text: Policeman has hours in helicopter

indicators.note: the officer has the letter within, holding it inside the word

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: An officer spends hours flying in a police helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: an informal name for a rotorcraft, from the chopping sound of its blades.

clue.text: Churchgoer in French capital dealt heroin

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: cards that are dealt are shuffled out, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A worshipper in Paris is caught dealing drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a member of a church congregation within a local parish.

clue.text: Swell certainly to consume gallons

indicators.note: consuming something takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sure, as in 'sure, I'll come', means certainly

explanation.surface: Drinking gallons will certainly make you bloated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rise and swell like a wave building up.

clue.text: Brilliant writer put at the top

parts.note: super means excellent or brilliant
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A great author gets top billing.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning: to write a name or heading on top of or above something else.

clue.text: Rise in endowment interrupted by decease

indicators.note: the endowment word is broken up by the other piece going inside

parts.note: a grant is a sum of money endowed or awarded
to decease is to die

explanation.surface: An endowment's increase is cut short by the benefactor's death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' is a noun: an upward slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a slope or incline, how steeply the ground goes up.

clue.text: Woodwind player, old boy is surrounded by books

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: the word is placed with the books around it

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A former pupil who plays in the orchestra sits among piles of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning: someone who plays the oboe, a double-reed woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Small military camp is not in position

parts.note: out is the opposite of in
a post is a position or job

explanation.surface: A little army base has been left out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning: a remote detachment of troops stationed away from the main force.

clue.text: Beer for hospital employee

definitions.meaning: a dark, strong ale once favoured by market workers
a worker who moves patients and equipment around a hospital

explanation.surface: Ale offered to a hospital worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a dark brown beer, and a hospital worker who wheels patients about.

clue.text: Valuable property like stations or plants

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as new'
to set something is to station or plant it in place

explanation.surface: Holdings such as power stations or factories are valuable property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stations or plants' suggests industry but is a verb: SETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things of value owned by a person or company.

clue.text: Think Dennis gets upset, being this, perhaps

definitions.text: Think Dennis gets upset, being this, perhaps

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of these two words are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses Dennis is easily hurt, given how he takes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works twice: the letters of THINK DENNIS rearrange to the answer, and someone who gets upset easily is exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: describes a person who is easily offended or hurt by criticism.

clue.text: New European friend's country

parts.note: pal means friend; the 's is read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A new European pal's homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Himalayan nation lying between India and China.

clue.text: Rural establishment a long way off motorway

parts.note: far means distant
M is used for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A country place far away from the main highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an agricultural holding with fields and buildings in the countryside.

clue.text: A grain seed

parts.note: corn is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A single grain of seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the nut of the oak tree, which is its seed.

clue.text: Obscure energy cuts end in catastrophe

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
clips means trims or cuts

indicators.note: the final letter is taken from the word that follows

explanation.surface: Power cuts end in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to overshadow or block from view, as the moon blocks the sun.

clue.text: Mess tart about in bed

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fools about with a tart in bed and makes a mess of crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Part for whole: the padded base on which you sleep, standing for the bed itself.

clue.text: Large, obese all round: the result of a blow-out?

indicators.note: the word for obese goes right round the other letter

parts.note: obese means fat
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big, overweight body after a huge feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow-out' suggests a huge meal, fitting 'obese', but means a burst tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tyre left deflated after it bursts, hence the question mark.
